source.title: Analyzing Populations of Neural Networks via Dynamical Model Embedding
source.authors: Jordan S. Cotler; K. Tai; Felipe Hern'andez; Blake Elias; David Sussillo

record.tranche_reason: The study measures model similarity and shows that the resulting clustering changes with the similarity loss and comparison method. This refines the claim about representation convergence by demonstrating metric sensitivity, but it does not test convergence with scale or capability.
record.gate_note: Included results that explicitly describe changes in model-similarity clustering under different losses or comparison methods, plus the reported within-cluster dynamical similarity. Excluded task-accuracy, extrapolation, and semi-supervised-learning results because they do not measure model-to-model representational similarity. No instructions addressed to an AI reader were present.
record.test_reason: DYNAMO is a meta-model method that embeds trained networks so they can be clustered, averaged and extrapolated. Every similarity result is a qualitative PCA plot of the study's own embeddings under its own settings: output-loss weight λ, L1 versus L2 hidden loss, and DYNAMO versus SVCCA. No result measures how aligned independently trained models' representations are, whether that alignment grows, or whether a convergence score depends on the metric. The λ and L1/L2 comparisons are framed as design choices of the method (λ trades off hidden-state against output emphasis; L1 is shown as a 'benefit'), not as fragility of a convergence measure. So the record's V6 links read a method-tuning result as a test of the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right, but the record overstates one point. The authors conclude that DYNAMO embeddings capture computationally relevant features of base models, and enable clustering that is less sensitive to reparameterization, model averaging, extrapolation and semi-supervised learning. They also conclude that sentiment-RNN embedding spaces form smoothly varying line attractors. They present the λ and L1/L2 choices as useful flexibility of the method, not as a caveat that the measured similarity is unreliable.
record.recipe_differences: DYNAMO learns model embeddings and a meta-model from hidden-state and output losses; it is not the original studies' representation-alignment or convergence measurement. The paper also compares DYNAMO qualitatively with SVCCA.
record.method_sensitivity: Clustering changes with output-loss weight λ, with hidden-state-only versus hidden-and-output comparisons, with L1 versus L2 hidden-representation distances, and with DYNAMO versus SVCCA-based distances. The reported cluster tightness also differs between the IMDB and AG News GRU collections.

fits_no_version.finding: Whether DYNAMO embeddings separate model populations (by data size or augmentation) depends on the output-loss weight λ and on the L1 versus L2 hidden distance. A pairwise SVCCA+MDS embedding shows less apparent structure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model-population clustering by similarity-based embeddings depends on the comparison loss and the target (hidden states versus outputs).

fits_no_version.finding: At λ=0, GRUs trained on AG News have more tightly clustered dynamical embeddings than GRUs trained on IMDB.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How similar independently trained networks' hidden dynamics are varies by task.

fits_no_version.finding: Sentiment RNNs within a DYNAMO cluster show geometrically similar line attractors. Attractor shape varies continuously with training-data fraction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Networks trained under the same conditions converge on topologically similar dynamical solutions (line attractors).

record.problems: Similarity and clustering outcomes are mainly qualitative descriptions of plotted embeddings; the study does not report numerical alignment scores or uncertainty for these comparisons. It does not test alignment as a function of model scale or capability.
record.rows_left_out: No directly relevant similarity-clustering result was left out. Task-accuracy and semi-supervised-learning results in Sections 4.2–4.3 were excluded because they do not measure model-to-model representational similarity.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep; no cross-architecture alignment measure.
Base models differ in seeds, but no shared-feature or subspace analysis across seeds.
The learned maps V_n from meta-model to base hidden states are not evaluated as base-to-base interchangeability. No stitching tests and no tests of relative or unpaired mappings.
No neuron, SAE-feature or circuit universality analysis.

No convergence or alignment score is computed under alternative metrics, neighbour counts or out-of-distribution inputs. Clustering changes under λ and L1/L2 are tuning choices of the study's own embedding method.
No measure of alignment level, plateau, or causes of alignment.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 'supports' labels are removed. All rows are qualitative descriptions of PCA plots of the study's own method, with no numerical similarity scores or uncertainty. The paper cites Li et al. (Convergent Learning) only in related work.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model scale or capability, and no test that alignment rises as independently trained models get larger or more capable.
The study analyzes model populations and dynamical similarities, but does not test whether different initializations learn shared features or subspaces.
The method trains a meta-model to emulate base models, but does not report a test of interchangeability by a simple map, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired mapping.
No test of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
Tests changes in clustering under selected hidden/output loss settings and L1 versus L2 distances, and compares with SVCCA. Does not test sensitivity to neighbour count or out-of-distribution inputs.
The study does not test whether alignment plateaus or whether shared training data or objectives, rather than a common model of reality, explain alignment.

rows.subject: ResNet-34 models trained on CIFAR-100 (collection; aggregate clustering result)
rows.operation_detail: Compared hidden representations and outputs using the DYNAMO embedding loss with output-loss weight λ = 1.
rows.measure: Separation of model embeddings by training dataset size
rows.value: Clear separation according to training dataset size
rows.note: The text reports clustering by dataset size; it does not give a numerical separation score.
rows.check: Shows that DYNAMO embeddings at λ=1 separate models by training-set size. This measures whether the method detects training differences, not representational convergence or a convergence score's metric dependence.

rows.value: Clear separation according to data augmentation policy

rows.subject: ResNet-34 models trained on CIFAR-100 (collection; aggregate clustering result)
rows.operation_detail: Compared hidden representations only using the DYNAMO embedding loss with output-loss weight λ = 0.
rows.measure: Separation of model embeddings by training dataset size
rows.baseline: λ = 1, where separation by dataset size is reported
rows.value: No detectable separation by training dataset size
rows.note: The text explicitly contrasts this result with the λ = 1 clustering.
rows.check: At λ=0 (hidden states only) there is no separation by dataset size. λ changes what is compared (hidden plus outputs versus hidden only), so this is not metric sensitivity of one convergence measure. It is qualitative only.

conditions.value: data augmentation policy: weak versus strong

rows.measure: Separation of model embeddings by data augmentation policy
rows.baseline: λ = 1, where clear separation is reported
rows.value: A weak clustering effect by data augmentation policy
rows.note: The text describes the clustering as weak under λ = 0.
rows.check: Weak augmentation clustering at λ=0 is a setting of the study's own method. It is not a convergence measure.

rows.subject: GRUs trained on IMDB sentiment classification and AG News classification (collections; comparative aggregate result)
rows.operation_detail: Compared DYNAMO model embeddings using hidden-state dynamics only, with output-loss weight λ = 0.

conditions.value: IMDB sentiment classification versus AG News classification

rows.value: AG News GRU embeddings are much more tightly coupled than the IMDB GRU embeddings
rows.note: The authors interpret the difference as indicating more similar dynamics among the AG News GRUs.
rows.check: AG News GRUs cluster more tightly than IMDB GRUs at λ=0 (Appendix B.3, Fig. 9). This is a qualitative comparison of within-task dynamical similarity in the method's embedding. It does not bear on any version's metric-dependence claim.

rows.subject: GRUs trained on the IMDB sentiment dataset (collection; aggregate clustering result)
rows.operation_detail: Compared pairwise representational distances using SVCCA and embedded the distance matrix with MDS.

conditions.value: SVCCA pairwise distances followed by MDS

rows.measure: Visibility of cluster structure among GRUs trained with varying training-set sizes
rows.value: The cluster structure is less apparent than in the DYNAMO representation
rows.note: The study reports a qualitative comparison, not numerical cluster scores.
rows.check: This compares the study's own method (DYNAMO) with SVCCA+MDS for visualising cluster structure. Such method-versus-baseline rows shouldn't be linked to claim versions.

rows.subject: ResNet-34 models trained on CIFAR-100 (collection; aggregate clustering result)
rows.operation_detail: Compared intermediate representations using the L1 distance in the hidden-state loss.
rows.measure: Separation of model embeddings by data augmentation policy
rows.value: Clearer separation between the two augmentation-policy groups than with L2

rows.check: L1 versus L2 in DYNAMO's hidden loss is presented as an improvement to the method's clustering (motivated by ReLU sparsity). It is a method-performance result, not a convergence-measure dependence.

rows.measure: Geometric similarity of line-attractor structures in hidden-state dynamics
rows.value: Line-attractor structures were geometrically similar for models within a cluster; the reported structures varied continuously between shorter, wider and taller, thinner attractors
rows.note: This is a dynamical-topology result, not a direct test of shared features or representation-distance convergence as defined in the claim versions.
rows.check: The link to none is correct: this is a line-attractor geometry result within DYNAMO clusters. It is qualitative and drawn from meta-model renderings, not from the base models directly.
